main_integration_review.scope: Main independently checked vocabulary/page locations, chapter boundaries, source emphasis spot-checks and cue scope/reuse. Original author-pending statements below are chronological draft notes superseded by this review. No clinical, human expert, recall or render validation.
main_integration_review.normalizations: Line-wrap hyphens, beta and punctuation normalized. Chapter23 wet surface expands wet or conducting surface; Chapter25 calcium gluconate expands Calcium chloride or gluconate; blood volume also appears as blood and plasma volume. Shared-word expansions are not contiguous quotations.
main_integration_review.family_collision_warning: Qualify co-occurring family cues such as atrial/ventricular fibrillation, calcium salts or gangrene subtypes; family reuse is not exact subtype discrimination.

source.verification: Initial author pass verified source hash, actual titles/references, original14 term/page matches and source rasters PDF85-89; PDF90 only the intentionally blank-page notice. 2026-10-20 expansion checks all55 term/page matches and font/annotation evidence in keyword_screen. Main independent audit pending. Vocabulary locations only, not clinical or recall validation.

scope: 55 offline vocabulary entries: 28 retained candidates, 11 reuses and 16 holds after main integration on 2026-10-20. Typography/key-term screen included; not exhaustive concepts, clinical teaching, measured recall or image prompts.

keyword_screen.method: fitz dict span review of PDF85-89 font names, bold flag16 and coordinates, cross-checked against previously inspected full-page source rasters. Includes MyriadPro-BlackSemiCn headings, MyriadPro-SemiboldCond section/table labels, MinionPro-Bold body terms and selected meaningful regular MyriadPro-Cond table cells. PDF85 only right column below actual Chapter21 title y191; PDF89 ends at REFERENCES. Short lexical terms extracted from emphasized Table21-1 clauses; treatment-effect verbs and complete clinical clauses are not candidates. Table21-2 leaf labels reviewed, with five selected unformatted procedure trials from Table21-3 rather than exhaustive procedure harvesting. Typography extraction does not exhaust all key concepts, nor establish measured salience. Main independently audits additions; no approval inferred from main's source spot-check.

highlight_annotation_check.note: fitz Page.annots checked all five source pages PDF85-89; no annotations of any type found. Printed/flattened emphasis may still exist; font/visual review handled that separately.

resolved_holds.resolution: 2026-10-20 author challenge accepted main-proposed cyan-eyed mannequin eye as an untested learned partial-name candidate. Original 2026-10-19 hold rejected cyan color alone as nonspecific and not a chemical appearance clue; that historical reason is preserved. New proposal adds familiar eye/eyed name material rather than demanding full syllable coverage. Audience cyan naming and contextual recall uncertain; main independent audit and shared hold-register integration pending.

entries.cue: Recognizable oxygen cylinder beside a transparent pressure chamber with its gauge pointing high.
entries.cue_scope: Oxygen plus increased-pressure setting name reminder
entries.reason: Preserves Chapter7 oxygen-cylinder/chamber family. Identity token only, not an installation, safety specification, pressure value, duration, indication or efficacy claim.

entries.cue: Transparent chamber model containing one conspicuous empty seat.
entries.reason: New occupancy composition using the established chamber ingredient. One seat is familiar place vocabulary, not an actual chamber layout, capacity standard, care arrangement or hardware specification; context supplies hyperbaric identity.

entries.cue: Transparent chamber model containing several conspicuous empty seats.
entries.reason: New paired occupancy composition with the same chamber/seat ingredients; changes quantity only. No exact seat count, clinical configuration, staffing, gas supply or equipment instructions implied.

entries.cue: Large gas bubble lodged in a transparent branching vessel model.
entries.reason: Same established bubble/vessel composition used for air embolism in Chapter7. No gas-species, arterial/venous, organ, cause, diagnostic finding or treatment distinction encoded.

entries.cue: Workshop vise opening its jaws beside a queasy-faced character.
entries.cue_scope: Release of compression plus sick-state phrase reminder
entries.reason: New release-action composition using an existing familiar compression object, without a limb mannequin. Queasy face is ordinary sick-word vocabulary, not a clinical presentation claim. Not a bubble mechanism, diving protocol, treatment or unique diagnosis; decompression recovery in a still image remains untested.

entries.cue: Limb mannequin compressed in a large vise.
entries.reason: Same singular/plural word-family cue, also reused in Chapter6. No duration, severity, syndrome definition, clinical fact or treatment plan encoded.

entries.cue: Overpacked closed compartment bulging around its contents beneath a high pressure gauge.
entries.cue_scope: Confined compartment under pressure category reminder
entries.reason: Preserves established compartment composition. No diagnostic pressure, mechanism, treatment, or assertion that all compartment syndromes are crush injuries.

entries.cue: Portable generator with exhaust trapped inside an enclosed miniature room.
entries.reason: Reuses the Chapter6 contextual cue; generator is not claimed as a new source statement in Chapter21. Not unique gas identification, a diagnosis, a current safety guideline or a treatment indication. Do not depict carbon monoxide itself as visible colored gas.

entries.cue: Mannequin eye with a conspicuously cyan iris.
entries.cue_scope: Cyan-eyed learned name reminder in an identified cyanide lesson
entries.reason: Main proposed cyan-eye(d); author challenged color naming, sound and object count and accepted the economical single-eye composition under the broad partial-name standard. Cyan pronunciation/naming and the eyed ending depend on teaching; not exact isolated recovery. Pure name wordplay, not chemical appearance, an eye finding, toxicity mechanism, diagnosis or poisoning qualifier. Historical color-only hold retained in resolved_holds; main audit pending.

entries.cue: Damaged lung model inside a transparent pressure chamber with a conspicuously high gauge.
entries.reason: Same learned whole cue, not a new variant. Gauge is a vocabulary ingredient, not a cause-specific model, pressure threshold, exposure advice or comprehensive physiology claim.

entries.cue: Recognizable oxygen cylinder beside a skull-and-crossbones warning token.
entries.cue_scope: Oxygen identity plus generic toxicity category reminder
entries.reason: New toxicity composition using the established oxygen-cylinder ingredient and a familiar hazard symbol. Warning token is mnemonic wordplay, not a real cylinder label, chemical classification, dose, exposure threshold, symptom or claim that ordinary oxygen use is toxic.

entries.cue: Air balloon outside a lung but inside a transparent chest shell.
entries.reason: Preserves Chapter3/7/13 singular/plural family. Balloon is a teaching token, not a foreign-body claim. No tension subtype, diagnostic criterion, causal relation or intervention encoded.

entries.cue: Worried character inside a cramped transparent booth.
entries.reason: New familiar situation composition, not a new emotion primitive. An identified lesson supplies the phrase; no diagnostic equivalence to claustrophobia, frequency, symptom checklist or management advice. Facial emotion recognition and recall remain untested.

entries.cue: Oxygen-cylinder character presenting an empty open wallet to a waiting bill collector.
entries.reason: Preserves the established whole cue and Chapter7 oxygen-cylinder primitive. Debt relation requires teaching; not a physiologic definition, clinical endpoint, payment claim or treatment instruction.

entries.cue: Oversized oxygen-cylinder study token beside a smaller matching token.
entries.reason: New size contrast with reused oxygen primitive. Not container capacity, a pressure relation, a physiologic definition, an efficacy claim or a target; learned context supplies oxygenation.

entries.cue: Skull-warning tokens emerging from a toy factory.
entries.reason: New production composition using the hazard ingredient. Not microbial biology, an oxygen effect, a toxin identity or any statement of what a treatment changes.

entries.cue: Familiar cartoon bacterium posed as a rigid statue.
entries.cue_scope: Bacterio plus static/still learned word bridge
entries.reason: New familiar static-state composition. Not literal bacterial behavior, a microbiology mechanism or an effect of oxygen; no organism or diagnosis identified.

entries.cue: Same cartoon bacterium token beneath a conspicuous cancellation cross.
entries.cue_scope: Bacterial identity plus learned cidal/cancellation category
entries.reason: New contrast composition with same bacterial primitive. Cancellation is learned wordplay, not a drug effect, kill mechanism, organism-specific property or equivalence to static.

entries.cue: Puffy bundle of familiar tissue paper.
entries.reason: New generic composition, not resolution of the earlier angioedema hold. Tissue-paper double meaning and puffy state need teaching; no bodily finding, cause, mechanism or equivalence among edema terms.
Tried angel at a building site for angio/genesis. Angel name/sound recovery is weak in this attempt; avoid adding vessel-growth prose or depicting a treatment mechanism instead of a name bridge.

entries.cue: Bone-shaped teaching token at a toy construction site.
entries.cue_scope: Established bone/osteo token plus creation/genesis reminder
entries.reason: New construction composition with existing bone ingredient. Learned lexical roots only, not bone physiology, treatment efficacy or a claim that calcium and osteogenesis are synonymous.

entries.cue: Torn cloth patch visibly being mended.
entries.reason: New familiar repair association, not a wound appearance, medical technique, mechanism, clinical outcome or assertion that all wounds require stitching.

entries.cue_scope: Lexical phrase extracted from emphasized clause
entries.reason: Tried flame token beside a replying character. Literal fire and speech response create ambiguity, so this attempt stays unresolved; no inflammatory mechanism or treatment-effect statement imported.

entries.cue: Spool of fibers beside a toy photocopier producing a matching spool picture.
entries.reason: New copying composition reusing fiber ingredient, not a new primitive or equivalence to fibrillation. Blast qualifier requires lesson context; not cell biology or an oxygen mechanism.

Tried closed/reopened supply tap plus damaged token. Too much sequencing and risk of turning the phrase into an ungated medical mechanism in this pass; preserve the useful ischemia ingredient without forcing a full compound cue.

entries.cue: Red-cell study token bending like a flexible rubber toy.
entries.cue_scope: Existing red-cell identity plus flexible-word action
entries.reason: New bending composition with reused red-cell ingredient. Not actual cell mechanics, a treatment effect, a measurement or an asserted causal relationship.

entries.cue_scope: Cell-name keyword from emphasized activity clause
entries.reason: Tried a white round study token; without an established learned identity it is too generic in this attempt. No cell function, bacterial action or clinical interpretation substituted for the name.

Tried capsule on a delivery cart. Transport is familiar but generic capsule provides little antibiotic identity in this attempt; no delivery-to-bacteria mechanism, drug fact or oxygen effect supplied.

Tried extending unresolved adenosine token with three generic phosphorus props; no useful base token and unnecessary prop pile. Existing adenosine hold preserved, not silently resolved or equated to this distinct name.
Tried oil bottle beside anonymous peroxide bottle; bottles do not recover the second identity without labels and risk chemical-process teaching. No useful economical bridge selected.

entries.cue: Eyeball teaching token beside a branching red tube stopped by a barrier.
entries.reason: New composition reusing eye ingredient, not the peeling detachment cue. Separate props are not connected anatomical structures. Central and precise retinal location depend on teaching; no diagnostic image, pathogenesis or treatment claim.

entries.cue: Ear token beside a sound-wave trail that ends abruptly.
entries.cue_scope: Hearing plus sudden loss reminder; sensorineural qualifier contextual
entries.reason: New familiar sound interruption association. Does not distinguish sensorineural from other hearing-loss categories alone; no duration, decibel criterion, finding, neural mechanism or treatment.

entries.cue: Red-cell study tokens spilling from a nearly empty pouch.
entries.cue_scope: Blood identity plus loss; exceptional/anemia supplied in lesson
entries.reason: New loss-state composition with existing tokens. Not blood volume, hemoglobin threshold, cause of anemia, actual bleeding depiction or clinical indication.

entries.cue: Limb model downstream of a closed red supply tap and visibly depleted supply tube.
entries.cue_scope: Existing ischemia family; acute/traumatic modifiers contextual
entries.reason: Same learned family cue; limb is a reminder token, not a claim all ischemias involve limbs or complete blockage. No trauma mechanism, timing, diagnostic criteria or treatment.

entries.cue: Charred cloth mannequin beside a flame token.
entries.cue_scope: Thermal/burn category reminder; acute qualifier contextual
entries.reason: New heat/damage composition using familiar cloth mannequin ingredients. Not a clinical appearance, severity, exposure amount, burn mechanism model or treatment recommendation.

Tried a dead-looking cloth puppet for necrotizing/soft tissue; death-state naming and infection recovery are weak and nonspecific in this attempt. No literal tissue appearance or pathophysiology imported.

Explicitly tried the same cloth/dead-puppet family, then a fascinator hat fragment for fasciitis. Unfamiliar hat naming and incomplete necrotizing identity weaken this attempt; no forced syllables or clinical definition. Original family remains unresolved.

entries.cue: Group of green street-gang figurines.
entries.reason: New familiar gang plus green association. Color names a wordplay ingredient, not tissue appearance, severity, organism, pathophysiology or a diagnosis. Pronunciation and gang recognition depend on the learner.

entries.cue: Same green street-gang figurines beside a generic gas-cylinder token.
entries.cue_scope: Gas plus established-in-this-bank gang/green name reminder
entries.reason: New composition with reused gangrene ingredient and familiar cylinder category. Not oxygen identity, actual gas production, visible gas, a microbial mechanism or medical appearance; no proprietary scene imported.

entries.cue: Group of green street-gang figurines.
entries.cue_scope: Gangrene family reminder within an already identified Fournier lesson
entries.reason: Explicit trial retains the same gang/green family without adding arbitrary four/near props. Fournier eponym is not encoded and needs teaching; not a claim of equivalence to gas gangrene or a unique diagnosis.

entries.cue_scope: Technical heading name, parenthetical gas gangrene tried separately
entries.reason: Tried closet fragment plus cloth/dead-puppet family; clostridial and myo recovery require too many weak fragments in this attempt. Parenthetical gas-gangrene name gets its own candidate, not a claimed full technical-name encoding.

entries.cue: Damaged generic teaching model inside a transparent pressure chamber with a high gauge.
entries.reason: New generalized composition removing the lung qualifier from established family. No particular organ, pressure threshold, cause-specific mechanism or clinical instruction; generic damage token needs contextual teaching.

entries.cue: Radiation-trefoil token beside a torn cloth mannequin.
entries.reason: New category composition with reused damage ingredient. Not an injury appearance, exposure threshold, actual radiologic hazard assessment, mechanism or treatment indication.

entries.cue_scope: Lexical phrase from unformatted table label
entries.reason: Tried torn cloth beside unsolved puzzle. Problem is too generic to add useful identity here; do not encode the table's selection/indication status or invent a wound classification.
Tried loose sewn patch and hanging fabric flap; graft and compromised remain ambiguous without more teaching. Avoid plant-graft/sewing prop pile or a surgical technique depiction.
Tried small bulging pouch inside skull model; abscess identity is not recognizable in this attempt. No actual pathology, imaging finding, clinical indication or mechanism substituted.
Tried bone token resisting a repair tool. Resisting does not recover refractory or myelitis economically here; no disease definition, treatment resistance criterion or guideline implication.
Tried bone beside radio and a death token. Familiar pieces become a forced three-part pile and may confuse radio with radiation; no full-name cue retained and no radiation mechanism asserted.

Tried tissue-paper puppet beside radio/death token; shares unresolved necrosis family and the radio/radiation ambiguity. No alternative symbol invented for the same family; no tissue pathology statement.

entries.cue: Limb model downstream of a closed red supply tap and visibly depleted supply tube.
entries.reason: Reuses same family for Table21-1 ischemia and ischemic-event wording in Table21-2. Limb is an identity token, not a location claim for every use or an assertion of complete blockage; no clinical definition.

entries.cue: Familiar desk fan with a conspicuous hand crank.
entries.reason: New composition using fan primitive without minute-clock qualifier. Not a ventilator specification, airflow setting, physiologic mechanism or procedure demonstration.

entries.cue: Loose tube beside a transparent chest-shell study model.
entries.cue_scope: Chest plus tube identity; placement contextual
entries.reason: New composition with existing chest-shell ingredient. Tube stays outside and separate, not an insertion-site, depth, indication or technical diagram.

entries.cue: Recognizable lumber plank with a conspicuous puncture hole.
entries.cue_scope: Lumber/lumbar learned sound bridge plus puncture
entries.reason: New familiar object/wordplay action, not exact pronunciation for every speaker or a medical site. No body, needle technique, complication or procedure instructions depicted.

entries.cue: Bronco looking through a familiar telescope.
entries.cue_scope: Existing bronco/broncho plus scope object reminder
entries.reason: New scope composition, not reuse of squeezing-hose bronchospasm cue. Same learned broncho primitive, not shared medical behavior or actual instrument use; ending and recall untested.

entries.cue: Familiar telescope inside a transparent open box.
entries.cue_scope: Endo/inside plus scope; GI qualifier supplied by lesson
entries.reason: New location composition with reused telescope ingredient. Not a unique procedure identifier, GI anatomy, instrument assembly or instructions; inside/root mapping requires teaching.
